Where it began

Justin Greaves was born in Barbados in 1994. At Combermere School he played in the same years as Kraigg Brathwaite and Jonathan Drakes. He went to the Under-19 World Cup in Australia in 2012 with West Indies, and in an earlier under-19 match against Sri Lanka he hit 90 from 68 balls batting at number seven.

English club cricket gave him some happy summers. In 2013 he made 109 and took four wickets on debut for Sefton Park in the Liverpool league, and by the end of the season had 742 runs at 67.45, plus 31 wickets, as they won their division. The next year he helped Frinton-on-Sea in Essex to promotion. His first-class debut came for the Combined Campuses and Colleges in 2013–14, and he first played for Barbados in January 2016.

The player

His one-day debut for West Indies came against Ireland in January 2022, and his first Test on 17 January 2024, against Australia, when he made 5 and 24. His first Test hundred, 115 not out against Bangladesh in Antigua, followed in November 2024.

Then came Christchurch. In the opening Test of the 2025–26 tour of New Zealand he was bowled for a duck in the first innings. In the second, with West Indies 458 behind and defeat looking certain, he faced 388 balls for 202 not out, sharing a stand of 196 with Shai Hope and an unbroken one of 180 with Kemar Roach. The match was saved and he was player of the match. West Indies' total was, at that point, the highest fourth-innings score in five-day Test history, and he was only the seventh man to make a double hundred in the fourth innings of a Test.

What made him special

Greaves offers a captain two players in one: a batsman with the stomach for ten hours of rearguard, and a bowler who can make life very quiet for batsmen. In the first Test against Pakistan, on 28 July 2026, he bowled five wicket maidens in a row, the first bowler in Test history to do so, going one better than Stuart Broad.

By November 2026 he had played 20 Tests, with 1,112 runs at 33.70, three hundreds, three fifties and a best of 202 not out. He had also taken 32 wickets at 29.56, his best 5 for 27, and held 22 catches.

Along the way

His path to Test cricket ran through plenty of white-ball cricket. He was picked for a Cricket West Indies B Team at the first Global T20 Canada in 2018, first played Twenty20 cricket in 2019, for the Barbados Tridents in the Caribbean Premier League, and later that year earned a place in the West Indies Emerging Team squad.

And finally

His greatest innings began, in a sense, with a duck. Bowled third ball first time round at Christchurch, he came back and batted for ten hours. It is a lesson for any young cricketer: a Test match gives you two goes, and the second one can be the one they remember.
